answer: Harness-attestation fingerprint bonding maps each identity to a hash of runtime, egress, and signing cadence, then charges a ferrous-backed bond per new hash and records its voyage through three-peer quorums. An attacker pays that bond per attempt, clears quorum, stays under a rate cap, and waits a fixed trust window while the orchard registry merges matching hashes; cloned agents thus collapse into one visible operator cluster and earn no separate trust before their bonds slash.
